task: Verify every factual claim on the landing page before it is published
principle: The page states facts to strangers who cannot check them. Nothing was written from memory; each claim below was read from a source on this date, and the counts are re-read from the live API at render time rather than typed into the copy.

live_numbers.method: Read from https://api.sterish.xyz/skills?limit=100 at render time (frontend/src/modules/landing/liveStats.ts). The values below are the snapshot used as a labelled fallback when the API does not answer.

derived.official_catalogue: 13 of 13 org.stellar.skills.* are SAFE and VERIFIED — zero exclusions
derived.fifth_dangerous: com.fixtures.demo.release-notes v2.0.0 — the rug pull, not a poisoned fixture

live_numbers.honesty_rule: CLAUDE.md forbids hiding the test namespaces silently. The page prints 'of 30 on chain' and names the 6 filtered entries, and liveStats falls back to 30 rather than to `total` when an older API omits chain_total, so no code path can assert the chain holds only what is shown. Covered by liveStats.test.ts.

rug_pull.claim: One skill, two versions: v1 Safe and VERIFIED, v2 Dangerous and refused a licence. Same name, different bytes.
rug_pull.guard: getRugPull() falls back to the dated snapshot if the chain ever stops saying SAFE and DANGEROUS, rather than rendering a story the chain contradicts.

cves.note: Both are published advisories, not our characterisation. Checked on 2026-09-20 before being put on a public page.

CVE-2025-54136.name: MCPoison
CVE-2025-54136.mechanism: Approval was remembered under an MCP entry's NAME; a later change to its command or arguments executed without a new prompt. An attacker commits a benign config to a shared repo, waits for approval, then swaps the payload.
CVE-2025-54136.why_it_is_on_the_page: It is the argument in one sentence. Approval bound to a name is exactly what Sterish replaces with approval bound to a content hash.

CVE-2025-6514.mechanism: OS command injection; the first documented case of full remote code execution on a client OS triggered by connecting to an untrusted MCP server.
